label: PF Backlog 622
title: Session isolation guard: never write outside the session's own working folder (hard ACL long-term + single-account alternative now)
body:
## Problem / why
A worker session can read/write files ANYWHERE on the machine - there is no enforced boundary at the session's
own working folder. During BI-PF-1325 a session amended a backlog item (BI-PF-1325) that exists only in ANOTHER
checkout (PF-features) by writing that checkout's file directly (the item was not present in the session's own
folder). All sessions currently run under ONE OS account, so filesystem ACLs cannot separate them today.

## Goal & value
A session can only affect its OWN working folder: cross-folder writes are prevented (long-term, hard) or at least
detected + reverted + escalated (now).

## In scope
- LONG-TERM (HARD): per-session OS identity (dedicated user / container / Windows AppContainer) whose ACL grants
  write ONLY inside the session's worktree; sibling folders read-only/denied. Requires a per-session identity.
- NOW (single account) - session-scope guard:
  (a) declare the session root (the worker worktree) via env (e.g. PF_SESSION_ROOT);
  (b) fail-closed on every PF/WorkerGrid-mediated write whose target is outside the root;
  (c) a git hook that refuses staged paths outside the root;
  (d) a filesystem watchdog that detects writes outside the root, reverts them, and raises an issue.
- Charter/AGENTS rule: never write/delete outside your own working folder.

## Out of scope
- Provisioning multiple OS users (environment setup; enables the long-term hard guard).

## Approach
Reuse existing owners (pre-commit/pre-push hooks, wired_audit, the WorkerGrid launcher); add a session-guard
module wired into the worker launcher + the write paths; design the ACL path now, implement it once a
per-session identity exists.

## Acceptance criteria
- A PF/WorkerGrid-mediated write outside the session root is refused; a raw-shell write is detected + reverted +
  an issue raised (watchdog).
- The pre-commit/pre-push hook fails on out-of-root staged paths.
- The rule is documented; the long-term ACL design is recorded.

## Risks
- A raw shell/file call bypasses an in-agent guard (soft) -> mitigated by the ACL long-term.
- Watchdog detect-after-write window -> documented.

## Open question (needs a design decision BEFORE implementing)
No per-session OS identity exists today (one account runs all sessions), so an ACL-per-user hard guard is NOT
possible yet. The "hard now" options must be reviewed/decided:
- container per session (WSL2/Docker) with ONLY the worktree bind-mounted RW (write elsewhere -> EPERM), or
- Windows AppContainer + a filesystem capability granting write only to the worktree.
Decide which (and how) before coding; ACL-per-user becomes the hard guard once sessions get their own identity.

## Related
Issue IS-PF-0050; IS-PF-0036 (one working tree per session).

analysis.implementation_strategy: Reuse core/guardrails.py, core/run_guard.py, core/write_safety.py: add a session-root resolver (env PF_SESSION_ROOT), fail-closed checks on WorkerGrid/PF-mediated write paths, and an fs watchdog that reverts+issues on raw-shell writes. Extend existing pre-commit/pre-push hooks and wired_audit. Wire session-guard module into the worker launcher. Design-only doc for the long-term ACL/container path.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES per-session identity provisioning (out-of-scope env setup) for the long-term hard ACL guard.
REQUIRES BI-PF-1370 resolution (merge/defer) to avoid duplicate guard wiring.
conflict_findings: Concurrent edits to core/write_safety.py and git hooks would conflict with any hook/guardrail-related tasks.
WorkerGrid launcher wiring may overlap with BI-PF-0428 runner setup work.
duplication_findings: BI-PF-1370 has ~identical title/scope (similarity 0.92) — likely duplicate; merge or define distinct deliverables before starting.
BI-PF-0428 (dedicated runner worktree) overlaps the one-worktree-per-session prerequisite.
BI-PF-1324 (unique scratch/temp names) partially reduces cross-session write collisions.
analysis.rationale: Prevents cross-session data corruption (real incident in BI-PF-1325) with high leverage reuse of existing guard/hook infrastructure; blocked only on the containment design choice and duplicate consolidation.
assumptions: All sessions still run under one OS account, so ACL-per-user is not yet implementable.
Existing hooks (pre-commit/pre-push) and wired_audit can host the out-of-root checks.
Worktree layout (IS-PF-0036) gives each session a unique, discoverable root.
risks: Raw shell/file API bypasses in-agent guard (soft-only now); residual window until hard ACL.
Watchdog detect-after-write window: damage visible before revert.
PF_SESSION_ROOT misconfiguration could lock out legitimate writes or false-positive block.
Watchdog revert may clobber legitimate concurrent changes.
evidence: Incident during BI-PF-1325: session wrote to PF-features checkout outside its own folder.
Candidate reuse modules exist: core/guardrails.py, core/run_guard.py, core/write_safety.py.
config/guardrail-policy.json already models guardrail policy entries.
missing_info: BLOCKING: decide hard-now containment: container-per-session (WSL2/Docker with RW-only worktree bind-mount) vs Windows AppContainer + filesystem capability.
Decide watchdog revert policy (git checkout vs backup-snapshot) and escalation channel (issue template).
Define PF_SESSION_ROOT contract (env var name, validation, override rules) and whether raw shell is even permitted.

context_review.reason: Components/files are explicitly 'Not specified'; only a high-level reuse-hint (hooks, wired_audit, WorkerGrid launcher) exists. The detection+revert mechanism for raw-shell writes is also undefined (how to detect an already-performed out-of-root write, how to revert, escalation target) — the 'write paths' to wrap are unnamed.
